prompts.display_text: Pin a country where President Thomas S. Monson announced a new temple at the October 2011 general conference.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country where President Thomas S. Monson announced a new temple at the October 2011 general conference.
prompts.citation: Thomas S. Monson, As We Meet Again, October 2011 general conference; ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org milestones
prompts.summary: Opening the October 2011 general conference, President Thomas S. Monson named six new temples: Barranquilla, Colombia; Durban, South Africa; Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo; Star Valley, Wyoming; a second Provo temple in the burned Provo Tabernacle; and Paris, France, the first temple for that country.

answers.name: United States of America
answers.fact: Provo City Center; Star Valley Wyoming.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Barranquilla Colombia.

answers.name: France
answers.fact: Paris France: President Monson said the Church was moving forward with plans for a Paris temple; Church sources date its announcement to this conference, 1 October 2011.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Durban South Africa.

answers.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
answers.fact: Kinshasa Democratic Republic of the Congo.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose second dedicated temple was dedicated between 1987 and 2000.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country whose second dedicated temple was dedicated between 1987 and 2000.
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and milestones, read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: A country's second temple, counting only temples now in operation, usually means the Church there has outgrown one temple. Germany's second, in Frankfurt, was dedicated on 28 August 1987, the earliest in this set.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Adelaide Australia (15 June 2000).

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Recife Brazil (15 December 2000).

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Toronto Ontario (25 August 1990).

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Preston England (7 June 1998).

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Colonia Juárez Chihuahua Mexico (6 March 1999).

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Frankfurt Germany (28 August 1987); Freiberg, dedicated in 1985 in then East Germany, was the first.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Fukuoka Japan (11 June 2000).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place named in Zechariah 9, from Damascus and Tyre to Gaza and Greece
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place named in Zechariah 9 (Hadrach, Damascus, Hamath, Tyre, Zidon, the Philistine cities, Greece)
prompts.summary: Zechariah 9 opens with a burden on Damascus and Hamath in Syria, on Tyre and Zidon, and on the Philistine cities of Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and Ashdod. The same chapter foretells the king coming lowly on an ass and names Greece, by its Hebrew name Javan, as a foe Judah will overcome.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Ashkelon, Ekron and Ashdod are Philistine cities in Israel (Zechariah 9:5-6).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Tyrus and Zidon are named, and Tyre will be devoured with fire (Zechariah 9:2-4).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: The burden falls on Damascus, and Hamath borders it (Zechariah 9:1-2).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Gaza shall be very sorrowful (Zechariah 9:5).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: The Lord will raise Zion's sons against thy sons, O Greece (Zechariah 9:13).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose main language got its first Pearl of Great Price between 1955 and 1979
prompts.text_original: A country or territory whose main local language got its first Pearl of Great Price (selections or full) between 1955 and 1979
prompts.citation: Church translations table, Pearl of Great Price; Global Histories chronologies: Japan, Tonga, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, Thailand
prompts.note: France, Belgium, Switzerland and French Polynesia are out (French from 1908); so is Norway (Norwegian from 1934).
prompts.summary: After 1950 the Pearl of Great Price spread into many new languages, often bound with the Doctrine and Covenants. Finnish and Japanese came in the mid-1950s, Tongan in 1959, Italian in 1965, Korean in 1968, Chinese and Samoan in 1976, Tahitian in 1978, and Indonesian and Thai in 1979.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: The Japanese Pearl of Great Price came out in Tokyo in 1955 with the Doctrine and Covenants (the translations table says 1957).

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: The first Korean Pearl of Great Price was published in 1968.

answers.name: China
answers.fact: Chinese, its main language, got its first Pearl of Great Price in April 1976, published in Hong Kong.

answers.name: Finland
answers.fact: The first Finnish Pearl of Great Price was published in 1955.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: The Chinese Pearl of Great Price was published in Hong Kong in April 1976.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: The translations table dates the first Italian Pearl of Great Price to 1965.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: The Tongan edition is dated 1959; the first 500 copies reached Nuku'alofa on 17 March 1960.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: The Chinese Pearl of Great Price reached Taipei in April 1976.

answers.name: Samoa
answers.fact: The Samoan Pearl of Great Price was published in 1976.

answers.name: American Samoa
answers.fact: Samoan is its main language; the Samoan Pearl of Great Price came out in 1976.

answers.name: Indonesia
answers.fact: The Indonesian Pearl of Great Price was published in 1979.

answers.name: Macau
answers.fact: Macau's chronology records the Chinese Pearl of Great Price of April 1976, printed in Hong Kong.

answers.name: North Korea
answers.fact: Korean, its main language, got its first Pearl of Great Price in 1968.

answers.name: San Marino
answers.fact: Italian, its main language, got its first Pearl of Great Price in 1965.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Thai translations of the Doctrine and Covenants and Pearl of Great Price were published in 1979.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Northern European country opened to missionaries with a prayer of dedication (or rededication), 1977-1998
prompts.text_original: Long after the first Scandinavian missions, Church leaders offered new dedicatory prayers across Northern Europe. A country in Northern Europe (the Nordic and Baltic countries, the United Kingdom and Ireland) that a Church leader dedicated or rededicated for the preaching of the gospel between 1977 and 1998.
prompts.note: Only Ireland counts. The 1985 dedication of the whole island was given in Northern Ireland; the United Kingdom had none.
prompts.summary: Between 1977 and 1998 Church leaders dedicated or rededicated six Northern European lands. Joseph B. Wirthlin dedicated Iceland in 1977 and Neal A. Maxwell dedicated Ireland in 1985. As the Soviet Union opened, Apostles dedicated Estonia in 1990 and Latvia and Lithuania in 1993, and Thomas S. Monson rededicated Denmark in 1998.

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Thomas S. Monson of the First Presidency rededicated Denmark in 1998.

answers.name: Ireland
answers.fact: Elder Neal A. Maxwell dedicated Ireland near the site of the first Irish baptism, October 23, 1985.

answers.name: Estonia
answers.fact: Elder Russell M. Nelson dedicated Estonia above the Tallinn song festival grounds, April 25, 1990.

answers.name: Iceland
answers.fact: Elder Joseph B. Wirthlin, then a Seventy, dedicated Iceland from Oskjuhlid in Reykjavik, September 18, 1977.

answers.name: Lithuania
answers.fact: Elder M. Russell Ballard dedicated Lithuania in Vilnius, February 20, 1993.

answers.name: Latvia
answers.fact: Elder James E. Faust dedicated Latvia at Jurmala, March 17, 1993.
